name: DomainEvent
purpose: Records an immutable fact about something meaningful that happened in the domain and can be published to downstream consumers.
invariants: A DomainEvent MUST be immutable after publication; mutation or retroactive edit is FORBIDDEN.
event_id MUST be globally unique and stable so idempotent consumers can dedupe reliably.
The event NEVER carries commands or intents; it only states that something already happened.
version SHALL increment per aggregate and serve as the ordering key within one aggregate stream.
extension_contract: New event types extend DomainEvent by subclassing a frozen event base and registering the schema with the event registry via a register call; schema evolution adds fields through additive versions, CANNOT remove or rename fields without a new event type.

sources.locator: Chapter 8, Domain Events (later-adopted glossary, reinforced in reprints)
Chapter 5, Event-driven architecture, event structure, pp. 162-170

why_essential: Without a shared primitive, each tool invents its own payload shape and identifier strategy, breaking cross-service replay, deduplication, and audit traceability.
alternatives_considered: Integration-only messages: miss the domain semantics and couple to transport.
Bare payload dicts: no stable identity, ordering, or schema contract.
CRUD notifications: leak storage shape and lose intent.
